text:
Yasmine: hey team, first-day headache  VPN connects but I can't resolve internal hostnames (e.g. `bastion.redwood.internal`). I can ssh to the IP directly, but `ssh bastion` fails with 'Name or service not known'. Windows 11, redwood-vpn client. anyone seen this?

Jorge: welcome! this is usually split-tunnel DNS. run `nslookup bastion.redwood.internal` and check the 'Server:' line to see which DNS answered.

Yasmine: ran it, shows my ISP DNS (1.1.1.1). if I do `nslookup bastion.redwood.internal 10.10.0.2` (the corp DNS) it returns the IP, so corp DNS works but the client isn't pushing it to Windows resolver.

Nisha: yep. On Windows the resolver can be stubborn. If you're on WireGuard (redwood-vpn is WG under the hood) make sure the tunnel config has `DNS = 10.10.0.2` and that you allow the client to update Windows DNS when it prompts.

Yasmine: where do I set that in the GUI?

Alex: Open WireGuard UI -> Edit tunnel -> add `DNS = 10.10.0.2` in the config block, save, then disconnect/reconnect. Also check Network Connections -> adapter -> IPv4 properties -> DNS suffix/search order. If WSL2 is installed you'll need to push DNS into WSL separately.

Yasmine: added the DNS line and reconnected. `nslookup` now shows 10.10.0.2 as the server and `ssh bastion` works. thanks! 

Yasmine: one more: I use Docker Desktop + WSL2. docker pulls from our internal registry still fail inside WSL with 'temporary failure in name resolution'. windows cmd `curl` works.

Jorge: WSL2 has its own /etc/resolv.conf generated at startup. To make DNS sticky: create `/etc/wsl.conf` with:

```
[network]
generateResolvConf = false
```

then remove `/etc/resolv.conf` and create a new one with `nameserver 10.10.0.2`, then `wsl --shutdown` and reopen your distro. That forces WSL to use corp DNS.

Yasmine: did that, restarted WSL, `nslookup` inside WSL now uses corp DNS and `docker pull internal.registry.redwood/my-image` works.

Nisha: great. two follow-ups: 1) we'll add WG DNS fix + WSL steps to the onboarding doc; 2) for customers on OpenVPN the equivalent is enabling 'Use default gateway on remote network' or adding the DNS suffix on the adapter.

Infra-bot: INFRA-4922 created: "WireGuard Windows DNS + WSL onboarding improvements" (https://redwood.internal/infra/4922). Onboarding doc updated (automated).

Yasmine: awesome, who should I ping if I want the VPN to always push DNS (so end-users don't need to edit configs)?

Nisha: ping #infra with your client logs + region. We evaluate forcing DNS vs split-tunnel tradeoffs per region. I'll add a note on INFRA-4922 to track it.

Yasmine: thanks everyone. saving these steps in my onboarding checklist. :party_parrot:
